title: Presidential removal authority and statutory limits
shortTitle: Presidential removal authority and statutory limits
summary: Removal authority determines who may end an officer’s tenure and on what conditions, affecting both supervision and institutional independence.
notes:
Myers invalidates Senate participation in removal of a first-class postmaster. Humphrey’s Executor upholds the FTC’s specified-cause protection based on the commission’s functions and statutory design. Wiener infers protection from an adjudicatory mission despite statutory silence. Morrison asks whether good-cause protection impairs the President’s constitutional functions and upholds the independent counsel arrangement.

Keep distinct the identity of the removing actor, substantive grounds for removal, procedural requirements, and remedies. A fixed term does not by itself resolve every removal question. Bowsher concerns Congress’s own retained removal role, which differs from a law restricting presidential removal. The September materials end at the transition to Roberts Court doctrine. Trump v. Slaughter (2026) then overruled Humphrey’s Executor for the FTC and rejected a multimember-expert-agency exception; read the Slaughter account before stating current law.
